**Shared-utility strategy & import graph rules.** The dependency direction is strictly one-way: `main.js → [GameName]/index.js`, `[GameName]/* → ../shared/**` (upward only), and `shared/* → three + shared siblings`. No game folder ever imports another game folder, and nothing in `shared/` knows a game exists. That invariant is what makes the layer reusable: adding a second game later means dropping one new folder and repointing `main.js` — zero edits to `shared/`. All relative paths, no aliases, so Vite resolves everything without configuration surface area.

**Compliance statements.**
- **Anti-Lazy Directive:** every function I write will be fully implemented — no placeholder comments, no stubs, no "rest of logic" elisions. A file is only considered written when it executes; I will run the dev server and exercise the loop (input → physics → VFX → win/lose) before reporting done.
- **Strict Memory Management:** all dynamic objects are pre-allocated through `ObjectPool` / `ParticleManager`; the 500-particle hard cap is enforced *inside* the manager so no game can exceed it; hot paths (update/render loops) perform zero per-frame allocations; and every geometry, material, and texture created anywhere has an explicit `.dispose()` path driven by `Engine.js`'s teardown registry.
- **Sequential Output Protocol:** I proceed one step at a time on your trigger phrases — "Begin [Game Name]" → plan.md, "Plan approved" → full implementation, "continue" → resume from the exact character if output ever truncates mid-file.
